result.title: Lost in Delegation: Studying the Effectiveness of Task Orchestration in Generative Search
result.summary: LLMs have quickly evolved from models used in isolation to agentic systems that delegate tasks to external tools and other LLMs to solve complex assignments. This agentic augmentation has led to impressive capability gains. However, when and how delegation improves performance remains poorly understood. For example, it is unclear whether delegation helps when tasks involve post-cutoff information that the orchestrating LLM cannot reliably resolve from its own knowledge. In this work, we use purpose-built datasets with pre- and post-cutoff splits to compare various delegation modes. We find that delegation provides no consistent accuracy improvement over non-delegated setups, with effects varying across models and tasks. When tasks involve knowledge unavailable to the orchestrator, delegation can substantially degrade accuracy, while direct tool use with the same LLM performs much better. Our analysis identifies distorted delegated queries, inefficient tool use, and failures to preserve and use information between agents as recurring failure modes. These findings suggest that effective orchestration requires both well-calibrated delegation decisions and effective exchange of information between agents.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文用自建的 cutoff 前后切分数据集比较生成式搜索中多种委派（delegation）模式，发现委派相对非委派并无稳定准确率收益，在需要编排模型未知知识时会显著掉分，而同一模型直接调用工具更好，并归纳出委派查询失真、工具使用低效、代理间信息未保全与未使用等失败模式。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「中间环节改写后信息失真、下游未真正使用传递来的信息」这一诊断视角，可能为 LVR 中视觉旁路、latent 信息是否被答案实际取用以及多模块间贡献分配的评估提供类比与核查线索，但研究对象是文本代理编排，与视觉推理仅有远领域启发关系。
